# RS2 v2.0 EQUITY ANALYSIS — SharkNinja, Inc. (SN)

**T0 Price (2026-08-24):** $180.76 | **Shares:** 140,917,400 | **Market cap:** $25.472B
**Analyst:** RS2 framework | **Valuation date:** 2026-08-24

## SECTION 0 — EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & VERDICT

**Verdict: SELL / DO NOT INITIATE at $180.76.** This is a genuinely high-quality, fast-growing consumer brand, but the market is paying a price that embeds a decade of near-double-digit revenue compounding at an 8.5% discount rate. My central intrinsic value is **≈ $112/share** (probability-weighted **≈ $115**), a **~37% premium to intrinsic value** (margin of safety **−37%**).

**How I got there (numbers before narrative):**

| Scenario | Probability | 10-yr rev CAGR | Terminal margin | WACC / g | Equity value | Per share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bear | 25% | ~3.5% | 9.5% | 10.5% / 2.5% | $8.6B | **$61** |
| **Base** | **50%** | **~8.3%** | **11.5%** | **9.5% / 3.0%** | **$15.7B** | **$112** |
| Bull | 25% | ~9.6% | 12.5% | 9.0% / 3.5% | $22.5B | **$160** |
| **Probability-weighted** | | | | | | **≈ $115** |

**Why the gap is so large:** at $180.76 the stock trades at 27.8x **2026E adjusted** EPS and ~18.6x 2026E adjusted EBITDA. A reverse-DCF shows the current price implies either (a) ~11% revenue CAGR for a decade at 12% margins using a 9.5% discount rate (revenue ≈ $22B by 2035, ~3.5x today), or (b) an 8.5% discount rate — a "quality-compounder" multiple — combined with ~9% decade growth. Both are aggressive for a **hard-goods, one-time-purchase appliance maker in a flat underlying market whose own CEO publicly doubts the durability of its double-digit growth** (Q2 2026 call, [Actual]). The sell-side mean target of $209.56 [Aggregator] simply capitalizes the current growth at ~26–28x forward earnings; it does not survive a cash-flow test at a risk-appropriate discount rate.

**Key judgment calls:** (1) growth fades from the guided +16.4% (2026) to ~3.5% terminal over a decade — beyond the one guided year this is [Assumption], and I show the range rather than pick silently; (2) I discount FCFE at 9.5% WACC (near-cost-of-equity given ~3% debt weight); (3) I use GAAP margins (SBC already expensed), not the higher adjusted figures management guides to; (4) I treat the $247.1M tariff refund as a 2026 one-off that does not recur. Under the most generous plausible quality-treatment (WACC 8.5%, ~9% decade growth, 12.5% margins), value reaches ~$160 — still **below** the current price. There is no scenario in my range that supports $180.76.

## SECTION 1 — BUSINESS & COMPETITIVE POSITION (MOAT ASSESSMENT)

**What SN is:** a design-led small-appliance company selling under two brands (Shark = floor care/cleaning, home environment, beauty; Ninja = cooking, food prep, frozen treats). FY2025 revenue $6.399B [Filed], TTM $6.910B [Filed]. Q2 2026 mix: Cleaning $522M (+4.1%), Cooking & Beverage $499M (+36.5%), Food Prep $459M (+13.3%), Beauty & Home Environment $286M (+65.3%) [Actual — Q2 2026 call]. International = 36% of sales, growing 36.6% YoY vs domestic +15.5% [Actual].

**Moat — real but narrower than the multiple implies:**
- **Genuine strengths [Actual/company assertions]:** 13 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth; category-creation history (Ninja CREAMi, Shark FlexStyle, ChillPill); entry into its 41st subcategory; TAM claimed at $125–130B; expanding adjusted EBITDA margin (guide to 19.5–20.5% growth in 2026); operating-expense leverage 5 straight quarters; low capex intensity (~2.5% of revenue); strong retail partnerships (incl. new Ulta rollout) and fast-growing TikTok Shop/social commerce.
- **Structural weaknesses:** **one-time hardware purchases with no recurring revenue stream** — this is the defining moat limitation for a DCF; product-cycle risk (a CREAMi or FlexStyle boom can fade as fast as it arrived); **flat underlying market** (CEO's own words); intense competition (iRobot, Whirlpool, Dyson, and private-label). 
- **Working-capital flag:** receivables are $1.667B = **26% of revenue (~95 days DSO)** [Filed, FY2025] — unusually high for consumer hard goods and a legitimate short-thesis/data-quality watch item. Inventory $1.002B (15.7% of revenue).
- **Governance overhang:** Grizzly Research short report (Nov 2024) alleged conflicts of interest and "insider enrichment" relating to the controlling Chinese chairman; the company disputed it; the stock fell to ~$94 then doubled to $180.76. Insider ownership 41.07% [Aggregator], short interest 12.9% of float [Aggregator] — this is a contested, governance-discounted name, and the short thesis has not been resolved in either direction.

**Data-integrity note on the moat narrative:** the deep-research brief in my pack is a second-hand narrative (not a filing) and overstates moat durability in places (e.g., its "moat durability supported by EBITDA expansion" is circular). I treat revenue, margin and cash-flow facts from SECTIONS 3–6 as authoritative; the qualitative brief as unverified color.

## SECTION 2 — FINANCIAL STATEMENT QUALITY & DATA INTEGRITY

**Quality of the underlying business (filing-derived):**
- **Piotroski F-score: 7/9** [Arithmetic] — high quality.
- **Accruals ratio: 0.0138** [Arithmetic, FY2025] — low accruals; most reported profit is cash-backed.
- **TTM cash conversion:** OCF $0.974B vs NI $0.695B [Filed] — FCF/NI = 1.16x over the last 12 months, strong.
- **Leverage:** LT debt + current portion = $0.736B vs $0.777B cash → essentially **zero net debt** [Filed]. Even adding operating leases ($0.165B), net debt is only ~$0.12B.
- **Balance sheet growth:** total assets $5.349B (2025) vs $3.295B (2022); equity $2.676B; retained earnings $1.610B — profitable compounding.
- **Share count:** +0.7% net issuance over 1 year, +0.5% 3-yr CAGR [Arithmetic] — modest dilution from SBC, but the company repurchased $100M in Q2 2026 at an average **$122.29** [Actual — 30% below today's price] under a new $750M authorization [Actual]. Going forward I hold shares roughly flat.

**Data-integrity issues I must flag (per pack):**
1. **Working-capital drag is a first-order input and is noisy.** Pack-computed "change in working capital" (+$0.343B 2024, +$0.723B 2025) is the balance-sheet delta of (current assets − current liabilities), which includes the cash build and non-operating items. The cash-flow-statement truth (OCF − NI − D&A − SBC) shows a WC/other cash drag of ~$0.20B (2024) and ~$0.25B (2025) — i.e., **~16–29% of incremental revenue**. I model incremental NWC at 22% fading to 12% of incremental revenue, mid-range of observed behavior.
2. **Capex definition:** filed capex ($0.146B FY2025) excludes capitalized software; vendor (incl. software) $0.160B. 2026 guidance $190–210M [Actual]. I use 2.5% of revenue, a middle ground.
3. **Segment detail absent** (XBRL dimension stripping) — no sum-of-the-parts possible; I value the whole.
4. **Tax rate withheld in pack:** I derive ~22% as my assumption (Q3-2025 ETR 22.6% [Actual, company PR]; FY2025 full-year appears lower; ~21% federal + state − international mix).
5. **Series continuity:** the 5-year revenue series (3.727 → 3.717 → 4.254 → 5.529 → 6.399) has no implausible steps; growth is real and corroborated by quarterly YoY comps in the pack and by company press. No basis-change suspicion.

**Overall: an unusually clean, cash-generative, low-leverage operator.** The quality is not the issue — the price is.

## SECTION 4 — VALUATION ENGINE SELECTION

**Primary engine: 10-year explicit FCFE DCF with Gordon terminal value.** I chose FCFE (not FCFF) because leverage is ~3% of capital — WACC ≈ cost of equity, so the two converge, and FCFE lets me use the company's actual net-income-based cash conversion. 

**Cash-flow definition — owner earnings to current shareholders:**
> **FCFE = GAAP Net Income + D&A − Capex − ΔNWC_operating** (SBC is already expensed inside GAAP NI and is **not** added back — this is the pack's own warning about owner-earnings overstated by starting from OCF; I deliberately do not credit SBC as cash available to existing holders, and I hold the share count flat rather than dilute it).

This is the conservative, dilution-aware convention. It produces 2026 FCFE of ~$0.54B — bracketed by actual FY2025 FCF of $0.488B [Filed] and TTM FCF of $0.805B [Filed], so the calibration is sane.

**Secondary cross-checks:** (1) forward P/E and EV/EBITDA multiples on guided figures; (2) reverse-DCF to state what the market price implies. I do not use a residual-income engine because book equity ($2.68B) is a poor value anchor for a brand-driven business, and I do not use a dividend-discount model (no dividend).

## SECTION 5 — DISCOUNT RATE DERIVATION

**Cost of equity (CAPM):**

- Equity risk premium: **4.3%** — Damodaran implied ERP for the S&P 500, 2026-08-01 [Actual]; I note a historical-average ERP (~5.0–5.5%) would raise CoE ~0.8–1.4pp. I use the implied figure as base and stress in §8.
- Beta: **1.168** [Aggregator — vendor window unknown; no pack code consumes it].
- **CoE = 4.70% + 1.168 × 4.3% = 9.7%.**

**Cost of debt:** ~**5.5% pre-tax** [Assumption — investment-grade-ish consumer co. at 4.7% Rf; SN's debt is modest]; tax rate **22%** [Assumption, §2] → after-tax ~4.3%.

**Capital structure (market-value):** E = $25.47B; D = $0.90B including leases (or $0.74B LT+current) → D/(D+E) ≈ 3.4%.

**WACC = 0.966 × 9.72% + 0.034 × 4.3% ≈ 9.5%.**

I use **9.5%** as the base discount rate. This is already generous to the equity (it sits below the pure CAPM CoE of 9.7% and ignores that a cyclical hard-goods stock with a governance overhang arguably deserves an ERP above the market implied level). The 8.5–10.5% range in §8 covers both the "quality compounder" and the "cyclical + ERP upgrade" views.

## SECTION 8 — SCENARIO & SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS

**The post-2026 path is the entire game, and it is unsourced by construction.** SN gives no multi-year guidance; the sell-side gives only 12-month targets; consensus next-year growth is 12.9% revenue / 16.2% EPS [Estimate]. I therefore stress the three unknowables — growth, margin, discount rate — rather than pretend to a point:

1. **Growth duration:** holding all else at base, if the fade is one year slower (i.e., ~9.5% decade CAGR instead of 8.3%), value rises ~$10–15 to ~$125. If the fade is one year faster, value falls to ~$100. A full decade at 10%+ CAGR (the market's implicit view) is required to reach the current price at a 9.5% discount rate — see §9 reverse-DCF.
2. **Working-capital intensity:** if incremental NWC runs at 30% of Δrevenue throughout (matching the worst observed year, driven by ~95-day DSO), base value falls ~8–10% to ~$103. If it normalizes to 10% (collections tightening as international scales), value rises to ~$125. **This is a live, trackable variable — receivables at 26% of revenue deserve quarterly monitoring.**
3. **Discount rate:** covered in §7 — the 8.5–10.5% band moves value from $134 to $92. The market is, in effect, applying ~8.5%.
4. **Margin:** the difference between GAAP 11.5% (my terminal) and adjusted ~13% is worth ~$15–20/share. I use GAAP deliberately (SBC-real-cost convention).

**Conclusion of the stress test:** no combination within a defensible range — short of assuming the market's own aggressive growth — supports $180.76. The burden of proof for the current price sits entirely on a decade of near-double-digit compounding at a below-market discount rate.

## SECTION 9 — CROSS-CHECKS & WHAT THE MARKET IS PRICING

**Multiple cross-check (current price):**
- Trailing GAAP P/E: **37.7x** [Aggregator] — rich for Consumer Cyclical hard goods.
- 2026E GAAP P/E: 25.47 / 0.78 ≈ **32.6x**; 2026E adjusted P/E: 180.76 / 6.50 ≈ **27.8x** (adjusted EPS guide $6.45–6.55 [Actual]).
- 2027E: revenue $8.42B (base), adjusted EPS ~$7.5–7.7 → forward P/E ~23–24x. PEG on 16% EPS growth ≈ **1.7x** — premium growth multiple.
- EV / 2026E adjusted EBITDA: 25.4 / 1.365 ≈ **18.6x** (EBITDA guide $1.36–1.37B [Actual]).
- Analyst targets [Aggregator]: low $195.67 / mean $209.56 / median $206 / high $240 — i.e., the sell-side is capitalizing forward adjusted EPS at ~26–28x. These targets are **not** corroborated by a cash-flow model at a risk-appropriate rate; they are an earnings-multiple extension of current momentum. My valuation does not defer to them; the pack's own data outranks them.

**Reverse-DCF — what $180.76 embeds:** at WACC 9.5%, g 3.0%, 12% terminal GAAP margins, the price implies a **~11% revenue CAGR for a decade** → ~$22B revenue in 2035 (~3.5x today, ~$56B market cap at a flat multiple). Equivalent alternative: **WACC 8.5% with ~9% decade growth.** Either way, the market is paying for a durable, near-Dyson-like brand re-rating. The CEO's own skepticism, the flat category, the ~95-day DSO, and a 12.9%-of-float short interest (i.e., a large, unresolved adversarial thesis) make that a demanding bet.

**Quality corroboration (why this isn't a blow-up short):** accruals 0.014, F-score 7/9, OCF>NI, zero net debt, $750M buyback authorization, cash $780M + $490M revolver. The bull case is real; the issue is price, not quality.

## SECTION 10 — RISKS & BEAR CASE

1. **Growth durability (biggest risk to my base, and biggest to the bull):** CEO's own admission; one-time hardware purchases; flat developed-market category. If growth fades to mid-single digits by 2028 (bear case), value ≈ $61.
2. **Working capital / channel:** receivables 26% of revenue (~95 DSO) — a top short-seller watch item. If receivables quality deteriorates or DSO widens, both earnings and cash flow are at risk. Counter-evidence: cash is up 300% YoY, OCF>NI on TTM.
3. **Tariffs / supply chain:** 12.5% rates on China, Vietnam, Thailand [Actual]; gross-margin pressure is recurring even after the $247.1M one-off refund.
4. **Governance:** unresolved Grizzly allegations (related-party/chairman conflicts); 41% insider control; stock fell ~50% on the report then recovered — binary, news-driven risk.
5. **Valuation / crowding:** short interest 12.9% of float with days-to-cover 5.26 — the stock is a squeeze-prone crowded trade; a "sell" thesis can be violently wrong in the short run. This is a reason to avoid initiating short exposure, not a reason to buy.
6. **Product cycle risk:** single-vendor blowout categories (CREAMi, ChillPill) can reverse; Q2 2026 already showed Cleaning decelerating to +4.1% [Actual].
7. **Share dilution:** net issuance +0.5–0.7%/yr before the new buyback; SBC ~$45M/yr [Filed].

## SECTION 11 — DATA LIMITATIONS & UNRESOLVED ITEMS

- **Working-capital drag is noisy** (balance-sheet vs cash-flow definitions differ); I used the cash-flow-statement measure (OCF − NI − D&A − SBC) to estimate 16–29% of incremental revenue. [Arithmetic]
- **Segment detail absent** (XBRL dimension stripping) — no sum-of-the-parts cross-check possible.
- **Capex definition** (capitalized software) unresolved between filed $146M and vendor $160M; 2026 guide $190–210M [Actual] resolves the forward path.
- **Beta** is vendor-sourced with unknown window/benchmark; I stress the discount rate broadly to absorb it.
- **Grizzly thesis** remains unresolved in either direction; treated as a risk overlay, not a valuation input.
- **Debt components:** I chose LT debt + current portion ($0.736B) for net debt, excluding operating leases ($0.165B, noted). Either choice changes value by <$1/share.

---

## SECTION 12 — FINAL EXECUTION OPINION

**Rating: SELL / DO NOT INITIATE.** Intrinsic value ≈ **$112/share** (probability-weighted ≈ $115, range $61–$160 across scenarios). At $180.76, the stock trades at a **~37% premium to intrinsic value** — negative margin of safety.

**The discipline:** this is a high-quality, cash-generative, low-leverage business that deserves a premium — but not this premium. The current price requires either a decade of ~11% revenue compounding at a 9.5% discount rate, or an 8.5% "quality-compounder" rate that the company's cyclicality, ~95-day receivables, and unresolved governance overhang do not yet justify. The sell-side's $206–240 targets are an earnings-multiple extension of current momentum, not a risk-adjusted cash-flow valuation.

**Action, if held:** reduce/sell into strength; the stock's momentum and 12.9% short interest mean the exit may take time and the trade can run against you — size accordingly, use the analyst-target support zone as an exit ladder.
**Action, if not held:** stand aside. Do not chase. There is no entry price here with a margin of safety.
**Where value becomes interesting:** a pullback toward **$110–130** (base-to-9.0%-WACC value) restores a 0–35% margin of safety; below **$100** the risk/reward turns clearly favorable for a quality grower at a cyclical price.
**What would change my mind (bull-case re-rating):** (1) evidence growth is durable — e.g., a full year of double-digit growth with Cleaning re-accelerating, not just new-category launches; (2) **working-capital normalization** — DSO below ~70 days with receivables falling toward ~20% of revenue, showing cash conversion structurally improving; (3) resolution or dissipation of the governance overhang; (4) a demonstrated 12.5%+ GAAP (not just adjusted) net margin at scale; and (5) management buying back stock near today's levels (their Q2 repurchase at $122.29, not $180, is telling). None of these are in place today.

**Monitor quarterly:** DSO and receivables as % of revenue; GAAP vs adjusted margin gap; international mix and margin; buyback pace vs SBC dilution; tariff actions; and the two working-capital line items that will most determine whether cash flow ever catches up with the earnings the market is paying for.

## 12.1 Valuation engine selection

**Engine: 5-year explicit FCFF DCF + perpetuity terminal value** — appropriate because (a) the company does not pay a dividend (DDM unusable), (b) the balance sheet is nearly unlevered (FCFF vs FCFE is a small distinction), and (c) the company's own forward guidance is denominated in adjusted EBITDA, which is the cleanest anchor for a cash-flow forecast.

**Cash-flow definition:** Unlevered free cash flow (FCFF), where:
- FCFF = (Adjusted EBITDA − SBC) × (1 − tax) after interest? No — FCFF is pre-interest. I model:
  **FCFF = EBIT × (1 − 22.5%) + D&A − capex − ΔWC**, where **EBIT = Adjusted EBITDA − SBC − D&A** (GAAP approximating EBIT, since adjusted EBITDA includes SBC within its add-backs).
